messages:
jess (SRE): heads up — p95/p99 for /v1/generate just spiked at 13:24 UTC. p95 went from ~140ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~420ms -> 3.9s. error rate still low (<0.5%) but tail latency is terrible. trace id: trace-0a3f9c2b
omar (oncall): oncall handoff — i'm jumping in. any recent deploys?
jess (SRE): no user-facing deploys in the last hour. infra autoscaler metrics show a small dip in available GPU capacity around 13:20 but not enough to explain p99. disk/io on host c-12 looks fine.
liam (infra): checking scheduler logs now. seeing a few long scheduling latencies (~10-15s) for model-worker pods, which could push up tail under high batching. also noticing kv-cache miss rate jumped for a subset of requests (cache-hit ~78% -> 45%).
maria (support): customers: 3 tickets flagged latency regressions, one on Dedicated EU region with high-importance. they're asking for ETA and mitigations.
jess (SRE): immediate mitigation plan we can try now (order matters):
  1) Enable model fallback for critical routes to fast-variant (minimal quality hit).
  2) Apply temporary stricter rate limits for non-paid/test tokens to preserve capacity.
  3) Turn on circuit breaker at edge to fail fast and return 429s for heavy clients hitting p99 repeatedly.
  4) Bump pool size for dedicated-inference-eu by +2 replica instances (hot path) and warm KV prefix cache.
  5) If still bad, scale traffic to other region fallback (us-west) for affected customers.
omar (oncall): +1. can we do 1 and 3 quickly?
liam (infra): doing 1 and 3 now. commands I'm running:

```bash
# enable fallback route for the api route 'prod/generate'
redwoodctl routes update prod/generate --fallback-model redwood-llama-7b-quant --fallback-strategy immediate

# set circuit breaker in the gateway for high-tail clients
redwoodctl gateway set-circuit-breaker --route prod/generate --trip-threshold 0.5 --latency-ms 2000 --window-seconds 60 --action rate-limit
```

maria (support): fyi adding notes to the three customer tickets: temporary fallback to faster model enabled and we may return 429 for heavy clients while we stabilize.

deploy-bot: submitted rollout change: route prod/generate -> fallback redwood-llama-7b-quant (change id ch-20260315-1701)

incident-bot: incident created: INC-20260315-08 - p99 latency regression on /v1/generate (channel: eng-sre, severity: high)

jess (SRE): liam, after fallback + circuit-breaker, please also do a quick config adjustment: lower batching window on the route from 40ms -> 12ms to reduce queueing latency. snippet:

```yaml
route: prod/generate
batching:
  enabled: true
  max_wait_ms: 12
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
```

liam (infra): applied batching change (applied via redwoodctl). warming KV cache: running a small prefix-warm job hitting top-100 prompt prefixes (job id warm-1798).
omar (oncall): monitoring dashboards — p95 dropped to ~320ms within 3m of changes, p99 down to ~1.1s. still above baseline but much better.
jess (SRE): good. next: longer-term / postmortem mitigations to add to playbook:
  - add automated detection rule: if p99 > 2s and p95 > 500ms for 5m, auto-enable fallback model + reduce max_batch_wait by 50% for 10m.
  - expose circuit-breaker metrics per-customer so support can see who got 429s.
  - add a cached-prefix warmup step to canary deploys for models (warm on new model instances before routing production traffic).
  - augment autoscaler to preferentially scale GPU-backed model-worker pools when KV cache miss rate > 30% under steady qps.

maria (support): can we craft a short templated message for affected customers with the mitigations and next steps? I'll send.
jess (SRE): yes, include: incident id, what we changed (fallback, rate-limits, batch window), what customers might see (short 429s for heavy clients or slightly different output when on fallback), and ETA for follow-up/root cause.
liam (infra): for RCA data collection: saving traces for the window 13:15-13:40, collecting scheduler logs, kv cache metrics, model worker CPU/GPU utilization, and network egress stats. I'll dump to the incident bucket and attach link when ready.
omar (oncall): rollback plan if fallback causes quality/regression complaints: revert route to primary model and instead ramp capacity + further tune batching, or roll to a canary of older runtime kernel.
jess (SRE): agreed. postmortem checklist items:
  - timeline of events and mitigation times
  - root cause hypothesis (kv cache miss storms + scheduling jitter + small autoscaler reaction)
  - action items w/ owners & target dates (autoscaler change, fallback automation, canary warmers, circuit-breaker dashboards)

maria (support): i've informed the EU customer that we enabled fallback and we're monitoring. they replied they're OK with fallback temporarily.

liam (infra): uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20260315-08/artifacts.tar.gz (contains traces, scheduler logs, metrics snapshots). attaching to incident.

jess (SRE): current status: mitigations in place, p99 stabilizing ~900-1100ms, keeping channel open. will schedule a 1hr post-incident review tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:
